name: ANSI/IEEE thermocouple with terminal board symbol
summary: IEEE-library thermocouple form that adds the head terminal board where element leads change to field cable.
description: This form adds the terminal board in the thermocouple head to the basic junction symbol. It is useful on loop and wiring diagrams because the terminal board marks the boundary between the element, which is replaced with the sensor, and the field extension cable, which stays in place.

Drawing the terminal board makes polarity at the changeover explicit, but it still does not tell you the thermocouple type or whether the head contains a transmitter. If a head-mounted transmitter is fitted, the output becomes a current loop and should be drawn as such.
readingNotes: Use the terminal numbers to check polarity at the head.
Confirm whether a head transmitter replaces the direct millivolt connection.
distinction: The terminal-board form shows the head connection point; the plain thermocouple form shows only the junction and leads.
